Area.evidence_source: The implications of these distinctions (neurotic, maladaptive, and clinical perfectionism) seem to be that high standards for performance are accompanied by a fear of failure, overly critical evaluations of one's behavior, and an inability to enjoy success. Such tendencies are more relevant to the maintenance of psychological problems as research has suggested. For example, Burns (1980) emphasized the role of perfectionism in psychopathology, arguing that for those whose standards are unrealistically high, the drive to excel can only be self-defeating. Pacht (1984) examined the debilitating nature of perfectionism, arguing that perfectionism is associated with a significant number of psychological problems; and Blatt (1995) referred to the maladaptive functions of perfectionism, including depression (Blatt & Zuroff, 1992) and suicidal behavior (Baumeister, 1990).
